headline: Explicit latent-process models replace naive assumptions in microbial and viral genomic inference
label: Explicit Latent Structure Inference
summary: New methods model hidden rates, sampling zeros and reverse mutations explicitly to improve inference from bacterial, microbial and pathogen genomic data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is replacing a simplifying assumption with an explicit model of an unobserved process. Neural posterior estimation infers gene-specific recombination and mutation rates in bacterial genomes via simulation. TestNet-PA treats sampling zeros in presence-absence data with an EM-based quasi-likelihood, aiming at better FDR control in co-occurrence networks. VENAS2 permits bidirectional mutations in spatiotemporal evolutionary networks, exposing SARS-CoV-2 reversions and hidden M. tuberculosis transmission links. The SARS-CoV-2 lineage work is less aligned, using graph-Laplacian spectral features with machine learning to estimate lineage growth rates rather than a generative latent model. What is new is the target: local, gene-level rates, zero-inflation and reversion are inferred directly rather than absorbed into noise.
